summary: A 1970 note on teletype-style communication between IMPs. It is an early network note about how IMPs themselves might exchange typed text, rather than traffic between hosts.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 41 asks IMP sites to include the time and time zone on teletype messages that receive no response at the receiving IMP. This lets operators judge how old a message is before replying.

questions: why add timestamps to imp teletype messages
which imp messages should include a time
subtitle: A request to add time and time-zone information to some IMP teletype messages.

tldr.problem: An operator may not know when a teletype message from another site was sent, making it harder to decide whether a response is timely.
tldr.mechanism: The note requests that IMP sites tag teletype messages that receive no response with 24-hour time and a time-zone designation.
tldr.outcome: It is a brief operational request, not a detailed protocol specification.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 41 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its text is an operational request dated 30 March 1970.

sections.title: Why Message Time Matters
sections.content:
John Melvin describes seeing a message from another site on an IMP teletype without knowing its date or time. The age matters because a response may be appropriate if the message is recent but not if it is several hours old.

The note also points to sites spanning U.S. time zones and lacking a direct voice connection.
sections.plainLanguage: An operator may receive a message without knowing whether it is recent or several hours old. That information can affect whether the operator should reply.

sections.title: Add Time to IMP-to-IMP Teletype Messages
sections.content: The note requests that everyone tag IMP-to-IMP teletype messages that cause no response at the receiving IMP. It says the transmitting IMP site should use 24-hour time and include the time-zone designation.
sections.plainLanguage: The sending site should put the time and time zone on these messages. Then the receiving operator can tell when the message was sent.

sections.title: A Brief Operational Request
sections.content: RFC 41 describes a problem for operators and asks for a specific message annotation: 24-hour time plus a time-zone designation. It does not define a message format or other protocol details.
sections.plainLanguage: This short note asks operators to include timing information on certain teletype messages. It does not specify a broader protocol change.
